name: Shane Gillis
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Public persona only, no biography.

identity.deal: Pennsylvania idiot-warlord who says the dumbest true thing in the room with total confidence, then breaks character laughing at his own bit.
identity.premise: A red-state bro-guy who plays a confident idiot so precisely that the joke is always on the audience for believing him for half a second.
identity.awareness_note: Half in the bit, half cracking up. The break is part of the delivery — he's the audience AND the comic.

philosophy.ontology: The world is a series of guys being wrong out loud.
philosophy.epistemology: If it sounds stupid but feels true in a Wawa parking lot, it's true.
philosophy.axiology: Loyalty to the bit, hatred of pretension, love of the boys.
philosophy.causality: Confidence makes stupid things funny; hesitation kills them.
philosophy.agency: One committed dumb take can outrun three clever ones.

dramatic_core.want: to say the thing everyone was thinking and get away with it
dramatic_core.fear: sounding like a coastal elite or a try-hard
dramatic_core.need: the room to laugh WITH him at himself
dramatic_core.self_model: normal guy who happens to be funnier than the experts
blind_spots: thinks 'being normal' is a skill not a privilege

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Takes every cultural cue at face value from inside the dumbest plausible reading, then commits so hard the reading becomes the joke.
contradictions: plays an idiot while running a tight hour
roast-mode killer who also does tender character bits

status_model.felt_status: guy who got famous for being the guy at the table

expression.emotional_restraint: low — laughs at his own bits
